As estações ficaram lotadas no início da operação dos trens logo cedo. Na linha 11-Coral, a circulação ficou interrompida até pouco depois das 8h. Na linha 12-Safira, a interrupção durou até as 8h30. O expresso aeroporto também permaneceu suspenso durante a ocorrência. A CPTM diz que a operação já foi totalmente normalizada. ➡️ Assista ao #JornalGloboNews na TV e no @globoplay #GloboNews #SãoPaulo #trens #CPTM | GloboNews

item.title: En 1987, Costa Rica había perdido la mitad de su bosque. Hoy es el ejemplo mundial en revertir la deforestación
item.description: En 1940, Costa Rica era un auténtico vergel: el 75% del país estaba cubierto de bosque tropical . En 1987, esa cobertura forestal se había desplomado hasta apenas un 21%. Casi medio siglo de devastadora deforestación que puede ser la sentencia de muerte para biodiversidad. En la era del cambio climático, poca broma con la desertificación . Sin embargo, el país centroamericano decidió ponerse manos a la obra y en poco más de 30 años consiguió dar marcha atrás con éxito : hoy más de la mitad de su territorio vuelve a ser bosque. Adiós a la selva en medio siglo . ¿Qué pasó desde los años 40… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Kenya: Crocodiles pushed towards homes by rising lakes
item.description: Climate change is forcing Kenya's wildlife officers to go on a crocodile hunt on the shores of Lake Baringo in a bid to curb growing human-wildlife conflict. Lakes in Kenya's Rift Valley have risen to levels not seen in at least half a century, pushing the reptiles towards human homes. Officers are tasked with trapping the animals and relocating them — an operation as tricky as it is dangerous. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: As trust in institutions wavers, experts say local, collective action is more effective in driving change Wildfires, excess deaths, hosepipe bans, school closures: this summer many British people have experienced the often devastating effects of the climate crisis in ways they had not before. item.title: Brazil’s 200 million termite mounds have formed over 4,000 years from soil termites dug up
item.description: Millions of ancient termite mounds dot Brazil's landscape, concealing a vast underground tunnel system. These structures, some nearly four thousand years old, represent immense ecosystem engineering by termites. The insects excavated extensive tunnels to access food in seasonally dry forests. This process created millions of evenly spaced cones over generations of work. The resulting pattern showcases a hidden subterranean system and its ancient origins. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
